title.justification: The title 'Neural Attentive Circuits' is directly provided at the beginning of the paper.

analysis.description: This paper introduces Neural Attentive Circuits (NACs), a novel general-purpose modular neural architecture that efficiently learns the parameterization and sparse connectivity of neural modules without domain-specific knowledge. The architecture comprises a circuit generator and executor, demonstrated to outperform strong baselines in low-shot adaptation and out-of-distribution robustness across various data modalities including image and text classification, point-cloud analysis, and symbolic processing.

type.justification: The paper presents empirical results demonstrating the performance of NACs across different datasets and compares it to existing models.

name.justification: The paper focuses on designing a new neural architecture (Neural Attentive Circuits) that can generalize across various domains.
name.quote: In this work, we propose Neural Attentive Circuits (NACs), an architecture that incorporates modular inductive biases while maintaining the versatility of general purpose models.

name.justification: The paper applies NACs on datasets that involve multiple data modalities, such as text, images, and symbolic data.
name.quote: We demonstrate qualitatively that NACs learn diverse and meaningful module configurations on the Natural Language and Visual Reasoning for Real (NLVR2) dataset without additional supervision.

name.justification: NACs are shown to perform well in low-shot adaptation scenarios, improving over existing models by about 10 percent.
name.quote: Quantitatively, we show that by incorporating modularity in this way, NACs improve upon a strong non-modular baseline in terms of low-shot adaptation on CIFAR and Caltech-UCSD Birds dataset (CUB) by about 10 percent.

name.justification: The paper evaluates NACs for their out-of-distribution robustness on Tiny ImageNet-R and finds improvements over baselines.
